header.title: Contract OS · Staff Product Manager
header.sub: How I own an AI product and plan its roadmap, for Dioptra.

blocks.h2: What AI product have I owned, and how did I plan the roadmap?
p: The AI product I have owned end to end is ARCS, a decision tool that labels every claim confirmed or unconfirmed. A user brings a consequential question. An LLM pipeline returns a recommendation with its reasoning, what is confirmed, what is not, and a confidence state.

I built it with Claude Code agents as my engineering team. Agents do what the spec says, not what I meant, so I write the acceptance test first. What I have not had is a human engineer pushing back on a decision; I expect Dioptra's team to.

What ARCS does not prove yet is the revenue side. With Contract OS I would tie every roadmap bet to a deal it wins or an expansion it unlocks, and learn which bets travel through Icertis's customers and which through Dioptra's own deals.

blocks.h2: Four decisions that shaped the roadmap
blocks.intro: Each with the reason it exists.

items.html: Code, not the model, sets the confidence state. Code maps the model's reported signals plus the user's stated stakes to a state. The model still supplies most of those inputs; checking them against something outside the model is the next step.
Trust is in the data model. Each answer stores its confirmed and unconfirmed claims and its computed state, so a user can reopen it later and see why. A claim nothing can verify stays unconfirmed.
Success is defined before shipping. Pass rules are frozen before a benchmark runs. Two of my own predictions were wrong, and the benchmark caught both.
Saying no is on the roadmap. The backlog records what is deliberately not built and why.

blocks.h2: How it is enforced, with real numbers

rows.v: One pre-registered benchmark, run once, thresholds frozen: 10 checks, 8 passed, 2 failed (an edited-text index at 85.0% against an 85% kill line, and a prefilter). Neither failure was adopted. The one new feature, a lineage index, shipped only after clearing its bar: a 69.9% wall-time cut.
Merges, deploys and publishes are logged to a ledger that refuses edits and deletes. A correction is a new row pointing at the one it replaces.
Which model handles which job lives in one config file; a pre-commit check blocks hardcoded model IDs.
Not yet measured end to end in ARCS. The one timing I have is a lookup cut from 5.15 s to 1.55 s. This is what I would learn from your team first.
Pre-registration and every result, failures included, are available on request.

blocks.h2: What I would do first on Contract OS
blocks.intro: A proposal to test, not a plan to impose.

items.html: Weeks 1 to 2: agree with Farah which decisions move to me first and which stay with her. Sit on customer calls with the legal engineers and trace one contract end to end through the systems that customer actually uses.
Week 3: learn how accuracy and unauthorized action rate are measured today, and who owns each eval.
Week 4: one written decision doc, argued with the founders before it is a decision: the next bet, the deal it serves, the metric it moves, and what we will not build.

blocks._doc: ROSETTA: translate your method into THEIR native register (their framework <-> yours). This is the trust move for a rigor-driven counterpart.
DEFENSIBILITY MATRIX: the 5 verbs x 4 proofings. Air-gap=grounded-external. Water=survives messy input. Fire=survives adversarial scrutiny. Bomb=antifragile (being wrong sharpens it).
ANTIFRAGILE CORE + LOSSLESS-TRANSLATION TEST. Prove being-wrong is the feature, then restate the whole thing in their vocabulary with zero loss.
